target_customer: Robot and machine manufacturers that need field deployment, repair and maintenance for their installed fleets
problem: Companies that build machines and robots get pulled into support calls and uptime problems at customer sites. Mantle owns field service and uptime directly so engineers do not have to.
business_model: full stack field service contracted by machine makers, pricing not stated
product_category: field service for robots and industrial machines

founders.name: Kieran White
previous_startups: Curo (YC F24), EV charging, acquired by Inspiration Mobility Group per the YC page
founders.background_notes: Per the YC launch post, joined Tesla at 18 and set up the European Model 3 service network.

founders.name: Graham Smith
previous_startups: Babylon (autonomous vertical farms), reported on the YC page as raising 22M dollars
Electronics repair business started at age 14
founders.background_notes: Not the healthcare company Babylon Health.

competitors.what: Robot service maintenance optimization software for field service technicians
competitors.traction_then: software launched May 2025, AI predictive analytics added February 2026

competitors.name: Formic
competitors.what: Robots as a service with deployment, field operations and maintenance for manufacturers

technical_complexity.rationale: A services business that needs trained technicians, dispatch software and robot knowledge across many machine types, more operational than technical.

defensibility.rationale: Service contracts and accumulated repair data could lock in customers, but field service is copyable by robot makers in house or by other service firms.

incumbents: Robot makers with in-house service teams
takeover_risk_then.outcome: Job postings in 2026 show robot makers such as RobCo and Diligent building their own field teams, which is the substitute Mantle must beat.

market_need_then: The company claims 500 billion dollars a year is spent keeping machines running in the US, its own figure. Robot makers hiring field service staff in 2026 shows the support burden is real.

branding.domain_note: No company website was listed on the YC page as of this research.

identity.voice_and_tone: The tagline calls it the pit crew for machines and robots

branding.brand_signature: The pit crew for machines and robots tagline

brand_strength.rationale: No site, no press and a name shared with a San Francisco metal 3D printing company also called Mantle, which was reported acquired in late 2025.

outcome_analysis: Mantle is a Fall 2026 company with no public traction, site or funding data yet. Both founders have built and sold or scaled earlier ventures in physical operations, which gives it founder market fit for a services business. The key uncertainty is whether robot makers outsource service or build their own teams, as 2026 job postings suggest some are doing.
notes: No company website exists on the YC page, so there was no site to fetch. Searches for funding returned only unrelated Mantle companies. A cross-check search did not find anything on Graham Smith, Babylon the farm company, or an acquisition of Curo, so those claims rest only on the YC page. Founder education is not listed. Team size 2.
